issues.extracted: Harvest Meadows Area TIF, section expenditure, category public safety, 1,816,062
issues.on_page: Budget schedule p20 prints 'Public Safety 1,816,062'; GAAP combining page p12 shows Harvest Meadows Area TIF with no revenue or expenditures and 'Interfund Transfers Out (1,816,062)'
issues.issue: [fixed 2026-10-21: kept printed line and total, added contra -1,816,062 public safety line and -1,816,062 other financing line; total includes other financing] The report's own GAAP statement shows this 1,816,062 is a transfer out, not public safety spending. Nonmajor GAAP public safety is 3,116,099 (p13), which is close to the other funds' budget-basis public safety lines (909,265 + 1,881,473 + 87,144 + 215,264 = 3,093,146) and leaves no room for 1,816,062 more. The receiving funds' Transfers In are already in detail (e.g. Street Projects 2,286,728, detail[107]), so the same money is counted as both spending and a transfer. Under the hidden-transfer rule, this should be a negative 'other financing' line (-1,816,062, split_from the p20 line and the p12 elimination, review), with the public safety spending at 0 or a contra line. The detail_totals entry for 1,816,062 stays as printed.

issues.on_page: Due in more than one year: Compensated Absences 774,296
issues.issue: Compensated absences are not debt. The current portion (liabilities[13]) is coded as accrued liabilities, but the noncurrent portion is coded as debt. Use accrued liabilities or other liabilities for both.
The page prints this under the Receivables heading, so 'receivables' may fit better. This is a judgment call.

Where the budget column prints a dash (zero), budget_final is sometimes null (detail[7], [9], [10], [17], [18], [19], [28], [40], [47], [62], [65], [66], [69], [70], [94], [95], [107], [108]) and sometimes 0 (detail[80], [87], [88]). A printed dash is a zero budget, so 0 would be the consistent choice.
